title: Memory-machine configuration guard
statement: Let $A$ be a memory-register program with $m$ registers and access to $d$ Boolean deciders, let $O$ be such an oracle, and let $D$ be a deterministic Turing machine with $k_D$ work tapes. Given a state map $q_0$ for the deciders, natural-number bounds $B,W,P$, an input bit string $x$, and a configuration $c$, the guard holds exactly when the deterministic program obtained from $A$ by replacing every nondeterministic choice with the answer $0$ satisfies the predicate $\mathrm{Pre}$ at bound $B$, input $x$, and the control/register component of $c$; moreover, every register value $v$ satisfies $|\mathrm{bits}(v+1)|\le W$, and the absolute value of the memory-head position is at most $P$.
